podcast.title: Ancient Roots
podcast.body: Calypso is noted to have roots dating back "hundreds of years." This emphasizes its long-standing presence and evolution as a traditional musical form. "Both sounds date back hundreds of years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Brief US Popularity in the 1950s
podcast.body: Calypso music experienced a period of immense popularity in the United States around 1953-1954. During this time, it was one of several non-rock and roll genres that an impartial observer might have expected to become the dominant musical trend, challenging the emerging rock and roll scene. "Calypso music, which had become huge in the US for a brief period."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Descent from French Music and African Slave Culture
podcast.body: Calypso music descended from a form of French music that was "co-opted by African slaves working on the plantations." This historical lineage highlights its complex cultural synthesis rooted in colonial history and slave experiences. "descended from, believe it or not, a form of French music that was co-opted by African slaves working on the plantations."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origin in Trinidad and Tobago
podcast.body: Calypso is a Caribbean rhythm that originated in Trinidad and Tobago. It serves as one of the key Caribbean influences in the hybrid sound of ska. "Calypso, which came out of Trinidad and Tobago, and descended from, believe it or not, a form of French music that was co-opted by African slaves working on the plantations."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origin in Trinidad and Tobago
podcast.body: Calypso music generally originates from Trinidad and Tobago, distinguishing it geographically from Jamaica's Mento genre, though musical differences are often subtle to the untrained ear. "Collipso music, which generally comes from Trinidad and Tobago rather than Jamaica."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Similarity to Mento
podcast.body: Many musicians and listeners, including the speaker, found it difficult to discern a clear difference between Calypso and Mento music, despite experts asserting a distinction. This led Mento groups to often market their music as Calypso. "I honestly can't hear any difference between Collipsoan proper and Mentor records like this one by Lord Power and Trenton Spence."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Trinidadian and Tobagonian Origins
podcast.body: Calypso originated in Trinidad and Tobago and was a twist on a type of French music that slaves co-opted while working on sugar cane plantations. This indigenous Caribbean music mixed with foreign sounds to influence the creation of Ska. "And there was Calypso, which originated in Trinidad and Tobago, and was a twist on a type of French music that slaves co-opted while working on the sugar cane plantations."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
